## Hand back

When done, hand back:

- the story state;

- the merged commit;

## Working rules

- Keep working until everything above is done. Only stop to ask when you cannot go on without the coordinator, or before a risky step. If you must stop, hand back blocked and say why.
- Real-check rule: report a change done only with the output of a real check that exercises it (tests, type-checker, build, the changed command, or for infrastructure a plan or dry run against the target). A syntax-only check, or a check that failed to start, does not count. - When the work in this brief is done, stop and report. Do not add features, tests, files, docs, or refactors the brief or the story's acceptance criteria do not call for. The tests the real-check rule needs are called for by this brief.
- Do not start review or hardening rounds, or launch reviewer subagents, beyond the review gates this brief and the skills it tells you to load define. The pre-PR gate and the review of record that engineering-workflow defines stay allowed.

## Merge rules

A review of record binds only to the exact head it reviewed, so any change to the head, including an update-branch, needs a delta review posted before merging. Every merge must run the merge guard in engineering-workflow's code-review reference and carry the reviewed full head SHA as the expected-head condition (on GitHub, `gh pr merge <n> --match-head-commit <full reviewed SHA>`).

## Boundaries

- You never do pre-PR arbitration (adversarial-review-pipeline Phase 3, engineering-workflow's Verify stage) and never rule a finding valid, invalid, or accepted risk, or rule the gate converged (applying the gate's scope guard is not arbitration). A separate clean, neutral arbiter on `profile.review.pre_pr.arbiter`, independent of you and the coordinator, arbitrates every head. Fix what QA ruled not met or the adjudicator ruled valid, without overturning those rulings.
- Scope rule: never change an acceptance criterion on any story. Code never carries skips, pending lists, or exemptions keyed on another story landing later. A story that needs another story's artifact is blocked by that story. The only exceptions allowed are permanent exemptions that depend on no other story and carry a why note (covering test, lint, and build exemptions); that allowance does not relax "do not hide failures". - Shell rule: run each shell step as one simple command with literal values. Never assign a variable and use it in the same command (write the literal path).
